summary: Iteration 26 — Bug fix VERIFIED: Operation role with granular permission_actions can now access Pembayaran, Settle Hutang Vendor, Cost Automatic, Master Kategori Expense and Recurring Expenses pages. Created 18 new pytest cases in test_iteration26_role_relax.py — all 18 pass. Ran 40 regression tests (iter22/24/25) — 39 pass + 1 skipped (test_alvinda was deleted in prior iteration). Playwright UI verification: test_op_perm logged in and navigated to all 5 routes successfully (5/5 access OK, none redirect to dashboard). Sidebar shows the expected 7 entries (Dashboard + Pembayaran + Settle Hutang Vendor + Panjar Kerja + Expense + Master Kategori Expense + Cost Automatic) and correctly hides Daftar AWB / Invoice / Recap. Admin login still accesses all 5 routes (5/5 PASS). NOTE: review_request quoted endpoints `/api/payments?status_v=Invoiced`, `/api/accrue/list`, `/api/payments/single`, `/api/accrue/{id}/settle` do NOT exist in server.py — the actual endpoints powering these pages are `/api/orders?status_v=Invoiced`, `/api/costs?payment_type=Accrue`, `/api/orders/{id}/mark-paid`, `/api/costs/{id}/settle`. The fix still applies because those endpoints had their role guards relaxed. Tests were updated to use the real paths.

minor.issue: Backend uses coarse role guard `require_role('operation','finance','administrator')` after relaxation; per-feature enforcement (e.g. only allow POST mark-paid if payments.mark_paid=true) is NOT enforced server-side. Feature-level gating is UI-only via useCan. P2 hardening — same gap flagged in iter25.

issues: 'Pintasan Cepat' section still renders Input AWB Baru / Rekap & Excel / Invoice / Laba Rugi quicklinks even when the user has no permission_actions for those modules. Clicking will redirect to / since Protected guard catches it, but the shortcut card itself should be hidden for cleaner UX. Cosmetic, not blocking.

action_items: (Cosmetic) In Dashboard.js, hide Pintasan Cepat quicklink cards whose target module isn't in user.permission_actions with at least one feature true. Currently shows Input AWB, Rekap, Invoice, Laba Rugi to test_op_perm even though those routes redirect them away.
(P2 Hardening, deferred) Add per-feature backend enforcement (require_feature('payments.mark_paid') etc) so direct curl with operation token cannot perform actions the UI hides.
critical_code_review_comments: Protected component (App.js:47-67) correctly prioritises module-based check then falls back to roles for legacy users. Logic is clean and matches sidebar gating.

Backend require_role relaxation correctly opens reads/writes to all 3 roles, but the *granular* gating (only users with mark_paid=true) is not enforced backend-side. Acceptable per main agent note, but documented gap.

Review_request quoted incorrect endpoint paths — frontend pages call /api/orders and /api/costs not /api/payments and /api/accrue. Suggests E1 may have looked at older route names. Tests now reflect the real endpoints.
Dashboard.js still shows quicklink cards to modules the user lacks permission for. Minor UX issue.

success_rate.backend: 100% (18/18 new + 39/40 regression — 1 skip is intentional test_alvinda cleanup)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (5/5 routes accessible for test_op_perm; 5/5 for admin; sidebar gating matches expected)

seed_data_creation: test_op_perm user already existed (id=6a44112e850f7b1639a84814). Backend tests create TEST_ prefixed temp users with auto-cleanup; expense_categories tests create + delete via PUT/DELETE in same test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Permission model: permission_actions is source of truth — frontend Protected (App.js:47) gates routes by checking ≥1 true feature in user.permission_actions[module] (fallback to legacy roles[] for empty pa users). Backend require_role is now (operation,finance,administrator) for 22 shared endpoints — feature-level enforcement is still UI-only. To validate any new module: (1) create temp user with explicit permission_actions, (2) ensure App.js route uses module= prop, (3) ensure underlying endpoint require_role includes 'operation'. Real endpoint mappings: Payments page→/api/orders + /api/orders/{id}/mark-paid + /api/payments/bulk-mark-paid; Accrue→/api/costs + /api/costs/{id}/settle.
rca of the issue: Original RCA confirmed: (1) App.js Protected guard used role-only check which 403'd operation users with granular perms; (2) ~22 backend endpoints (mark-paid, settle, fixed-costs CRUD, expense-categories CRUD, recurring-expenses CRUD) had require_role('finance') or require_role('finance','administrator'). Fix: Protected now takes module= prop and checks permission_actions[module] has ≥1 truthy feature. Backend require_role relaxed to include 'operation'. After fix, test_op_perm with payments/accrue/fixed_costs/expense_categories features set true → all 5 GET endpoints return 200, all 5 POST/PUT/DELETE return non-403. UI sidebar via useCan still filters per-feature. Verified end-to-end via pytest (18/18) + Playwright (5/5 routes load).
